solution: Move {=x} units along the horizontal axis — right if {=x} is positive, left if negative — to the vertical line $x = {=x}$.
From there, move {=y} units parallel to the vertical axis — up if {=y} is positive, down if negative.
Mark the point where the two moves end: this is $({=x}, {=y})$.
notes: pair_plotter tests the 'given coordinates, locate the point' half of this LO — the same direction as the three MCQ anchors (ex8-1-3, ex8-1-4, ex8-6-2), which all ask 'which point lies at (x, y)'. The fourth anchor (ex8-1-1, 'find the coordinates of point D') runs the opposite direction — reading coordinates off a plotted, lettered point in a diagram — and no existing kind can pose that: every kind here grades a construction the student builds from a stated target, not a reading-off of a figure the student never sees (per the no-figure-in-stem rule, we can't even show the diagram). That reading-direction half of the LO is therefore left untested by this widget; instances still use its answer, (3, 3), since it is a valid lattice target for the placing direction.
